sentences.text:
1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E. V. Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.13058 Of 2018
O R D E R:

The present Criminal Petition is filed seeking to quash the proceedings initiated against the petitioner in F.I.R.No.114 of 2016 in C.C.No.721 of 2016 on the file of the learned VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, at Rajendra Nagar, Cyberabad (for short, "the trial Court") for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 506 of I.P.C.
2.

entities.text: VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, at Rajendra Nagar, Cyberabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Ms.Seema Yasmeen, learned counsel representing Mr.Vikram Chandra, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.Vizarath Ali, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.2-State.

Despite notice, there is no representation on behalf of respondent No.1.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner/accused was alleged to have borrowed an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- from respondent No.1/complainant and issued four (4) post dated cheques as a security.
It is stated that on presentation, by the complainant, the said cheques were returned dishonoured for the reason "insufficient funds".

Therefore, respondent No.1 filed a criminal complaint vide C.C.No.10 of 2017 on the file of the learned V Special Metropolitan Magistrate, at Hyderabad against the petitioner for the offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act (for short, "the NI Act").

It is further stated that another case was also registered against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 420 and 506 of I.P.C. vide C.C.No.721 of 2016 on the file of the learned VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, at Rajendra Nagar,
Cyberabad.

entities.text:
VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, at Rajendra Nagar,
Cyberabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted that the petitioner and respondent No.1 had compromised the matter in front of the elders and respondent No.1 agreed to withdraw both the cases filed against the petitioner, by receiving the due amount.

Pursuant thereto, the petitioner paid the due amount of Rs.4,00,000/-
and issued two demand drafts vide D.D.Nos.566651 and 566652, dated 09.05.2018 in favour of respondent No.1 and the C.C.No.10 of 2017 was withdrawn vide order dated 10.05.2018 in Crl.M.P.No.1378 of 2018 in C.C.No.10 of 2017.

However, after receipt of the due amount,
respondent No.1 failed to withdraw the C.C.No.721 of 2016 pending before the trial Court.

Hence,
the petitioner filed the present Criminal Petition seeking to quash the impugned proceedings.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that after receipt of the amount due, respondent No.1 had intentionally failed to withdraw the C.C.No.721 of 2016 only to harass the petitioner in order to extract more money which is abuse of process of law.
Therefore, she seeks to quash the impugned proceedings.

sentences.text:
A perusal of the receipt dated 10.05.2018 filed along with the Revision would show that respondent No.1 had acknowledged the receipt of the amount of Rs.4,00,000/- towards the full and final settlement of the case in C.C.No.10 of 2017 and the same remains valid towards the settlement arrived at by the parties in Crime No.114 of 2016 in C.C.No.721 of 2016 before the trial Court.
7.

In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and upon taking into consideration the decisions passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Prem Chand Sing Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh 1 and another and Babubhai Vs. State of Gujarat and others 2 this Court, is of the opinion that the substratum of the two proceedings/F.I.R.s is common in nature.

sentences.text: Mere addition of 1 (2020) 3 Supreme Court Cases 54 (2010) 12 Supreme Court Cases 254 charges under different sections of law in the impugned F.I.R. cannot be considered as different ingredient to justify the other F.I.R. as being based on different materials, allegations and grounds.

entities.text: 1 (2020) 3 Supreme Court Cases 54 (2010) 12 Supreme Court Cases 254
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Here there are two F.I.R.s registered in respect of same transaction.
The C.C.No.10 of 2017 was withdrawn as the matter was compromised between both the parties.

Therefore, any complaint in connection with the same or connected offences relating to the same incident or incidents which are parts of the same transaction is, in my considered view, not permissible under law.

8. Therefore, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner/accused in C.C.No.721 of 2016 on the file of the learned VIII Metropolitan Magistrate, at Rajendra Nagar, Cyberabad are hereby quashed.

opennyai_summary.arguments:

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and upon taking into consideration the decisions passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Prem Chand Sing Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh 1 and another and Babubhai Vs. State of Gujarat and others 2 this Court, is of the opinion that the substratum of the two proceedings/F.I.R.s is common in nature.
Mere addition of 1 (2020) 3 Supreme Court Cases 54 (2010) 12 Supreme Court Cases 254 charges under different sections of law in the impugned F.I.R. cannot be considered as different ingredient to justify the other F.I.R. as being based on different materials, allegations and grounds.
Here there are two F.I.R.s registered in respect of same transaction.
Therefore, any complaint in connection with the same or connected offences relating to the same incident or incidents which are parts of the same transaction is, in my considered view, not permissible under law.
